tone_statements.citation: Luri, Moses Dramani. 2023. Aspects of Sɩsaalɩ dialectology. International Journal of Novel Research and Development (IJNRD) 8(12): a782-a795. ISSN 2456-4184, paper ID IJNRD2312096.
tone_statements.quote: Phonologically, Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language and prominent among the functions of tone in Sɩsaalɩ is the fact that it brings about dialectal difference (example 2 &3) below: Example 2: data from Tumuluŋ dialect (2) a. bà:rà, bá:rá “roam, roamed” b. bá:rɛ́, bà:rá “go behind, went behind” […] The tone is also found to bring about grammatical difference: mark possession, mark number (example 4), mark tense (example 5) and indicate the type of sentence (statement or interrogative).
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 marked (high acute, low grave); no explicit inventory statement

tone_statements.quote: If the series is in focus, only the first verb takes focus tone. If the series is out of focus, all the verbs take non-focus tone. […] The negative particle ‘bɩ’ becomes ‘sɩ’. tone_statements.citation: Funke, Emil. 1922. Die Isala-Sprache im Westsudan. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen 25 (3. Abt., Afrikanische Studien): 69-87.
tone_statements.quote: p. 73, section "2. Töne.": "Außer dem dynamischen Ton wird ganz deutlich der sog. musikalische Silbenton unterschieden. Wenn auch im Isala die Fälle, in denen gleichlautende Wörter durch verschiedenen Ton ganz verschiedene Bedeutung erhalten, viel seltener zu sein scheinen als in manchen andern westafrikanischen Sprachen, so darf doch der Tonfall keineswegs geringfügig behandelt werden. Einige der wenigen Beispiele, in denen unterschiedlicher Ton auch unterschiedliche Bedeutung bewirkt, sind: nâse Hand násé Fuß (Die Stammwörter sind hier nâ bzw. ná.) ǹkídé (ǹkídá) das meinige ǹkídà »nicht das meinige« = das seinige. Die Tonbezeichnung ist die übliche: nämlich: ´ (á) für Hochton ` (à) » Tiefton [third mark] (a) » Mittelton [two marks] » die zusammengesetzten Töne: (ǎ u. â) tiefhoch und hochtief. In der Regel ist die Anfangssilbe nicht mit einem Tonzeichen versehen, wenn sie tieftonig ist." p. 74 (plural suffix -ba): "Da das Suffix »ba« ausgesprochen mitteltonig ist, so bringt es der Tonfall mit sich, daß die voraufgehende Silbe in der Regel hochtonig wird. Es zieht also in vielen Fällen den Hochton, der meist auch zugleich der Starkton eines Wortes ist, nach sich."
tone_statements.locator: printed pp. 73-74; section 'Die Laute und Töne des Isala' opens on p. 70
tone_statements.check: quotation from the author's open copy, read 2026-09-25; not yet verified by a second reading
tone_statements.summary: Tone: the work states that 'musical syllable tone' is clearly distinguished besides the dynamic accent; tone minimal pairs exist but are said to be rarer than in some other West African languages (examples: nâse 'hand' vs násé 'foot'; ǹkídé 'mine' vs ǹkídà 'his'). Tone marks: high (acute), low (grave), mid (a third mark; glyph not certain from the scan), plus two compound tones low-high and high-l

tone.says: Introductory phonology section (1.2.3, pp. 3-5) states that Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language in which tone has lexical function (distinguishing otherwise identical words) and grammatical function (tense/aspect: present marked by low tone, past by high tone on the verb's final syllable; pronoun vs imperative distinctions), illustrated with Moran 2006: 94 examples; notes (after Rowland 1966, Blass 1975, Moran 2006) that low tone is usually left unmarked. sources.quote: Phonologically, Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language and prominent among the functions of tone in Sɩsaalɩ is the fact that it brings about dialectal difference (example 2 &3) below: Example 2: data from Tumuluŋ dialect (2) a. bà:rà, bá:rá “roam, roamed” b. bá:rɛ́, bà:rá “go behind, went behind” […] The tone is also found to bring about grammatical difference: mark possession, mark number (example 4), mark tense (example 5) and indicate the type of sentence (statement or interrogative).
sources.note: States that Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language; tone distinguishes dialects (verb tone patterns differ between Tumuluŋ and Bʋwaalɩ: bà:rà/bá:rá 'roam/roamed' etc.) and has grammatical functions: marks possession, number (ì 'you sg' vs í 'you pl'), tense/aspect and sentence type (statement vs interrogative). Only H (acute) and L (grave) marks are used; no inventory count, no downstep discussion; a short passage inside a dialect survey, not a tone analysis.
sources.venue: International Journal of Novel Research and Development (IJNRD)
